title: Hypoglycaemia at a 10K run
setting: Hot summer day 10K run. 25M runner staggering near catering stand, looking extremely pale, cold, clammy, behaving in a confused, grumpy, and argumentative manner.
verdictExplanation: Diabetic runner with blood glucose of 2.5 mmol/L, altered mental status (grumpy, confused), and autonomic symptoms (sweaty, pale). Sick: needs immediate glucose treatment.

shared.response: Responding but very confused and argumentative
shared.circulation: Extremely pale, cold, and clammy skin

history.history: Midway through a 10K run, missed breakfast and lunch, collapsed near catering area
history.additional: His friend says he has not eaten all day and is normally very friendly

followUp.question: What is the first-line treatment for this patient while he is still able to swallow?

options.text: Give 15-20g of fast-acting sugar (sugary drink, sweets, or gel) and reassess in 15 minutes
Administer his regular dose of insulin to stabilize his blood sugar
Encourage him to run to the finish line to complete the race
Lie him flat on his back, elevate his legs, and give him water

followUp.explanation: Symptomatic low blood sugar requires immediate fast-acting oral sugar. Giving insulin is highly dangerous and could be fatal. He must not continue the race. Water alone does not raise blood sugar.

evolvingStage.narrative: While waiting for the observations to stabilize, he becomes increasingly drowsy and floppy. He is lying on the ground, breathing, but only rouses briefly to pain, and cannot swallow.

followUp.question: He is now unresponsive and unable to swallow safely. What is your priority action?

options.text: Call 999 immediately, place him in the recovery position to protect the airway, and monitor breathing
Force glucose gel into his mouth and hold his head back to swallow
Administer an injection of insulin immediately
Wait another 10 minutes to see if he naturally wakes up

followUp.explanation: An unresponsive patient who is breathing must be placed in the recovery position to protect the airway. Never force liquids/gels into the mouth of someone who cannot swallow due to choking risk. Call 999 immediately.

levelFlags.cfaNotes: Recognize the signs of low blood sugar (irritable, sweaty, pale). Give sugary food/drink immediately if conscious. If unresponsive, recovery position and 999.
levelFlags.erNotes: Measure blood glucose. Treat with oral glucose if conscious. If unresponsive/unconscious, administer glucagon IM (if trained/authorized) or call 999 and protect the airway. Monitor vital signs.
